content: 1. Administer gentamicin at a dose of 5 mg/kg every 12 to 24 hours. Monitor serum concentrations regularly. Ensure peak levels are within 4-12 mg/L and trough levels are within 1-2 mg/L. 2. Monitor for nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity, and ototoxicity at the start of therapy and throughout treatment. Individualize dosing due to the narrow therapeutic index. 3. Use ideal body weight for dose calculations in mg/kg, except in neonates, where actual body weight should be used. 4. Gentamicin reduces the effects of agalsidase alfa and beta through pharmacodynamic antagonism. These combinations are contraindicated. 5. Co-administration of amphotericin B deoxycholate and gentamicin increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Gentamicin enhances the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Concurrent use of gentamicin and bacitracin increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid combining bacitracin with other nephrotoxic agents. 8. Gentamicin reduces the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines, such as the BCG vaccine, by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 9. Co-administration of bumetanide and gentamicin increases the risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Gentamicin reduces the efficacy of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration with systemic antibiotics, as they may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 11. Co-administration of cidofovir and gentamicin increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Gentamicin enhances the effects of cisatracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Co-administration of furosemide and gentamicin increases the risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 15. Gentamicin reduces the efficacy of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores. Antibiotics may decrease their effectiveness if co-administered. Complete antibiotic regimens 2-4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 16. Co-administration of gentamicin and neomycin (oral) increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity.
